declarations.name: InsightEvaluation
declarations.signature: final class InsightEvaluation<each InsightResult> where repeat each InsightResult : TrustInsight
declarations.comment:
Result object for ``InsightEvaluator/requestEvaluation(context:)``

There two ways to access the information. The most secure approach is to send the ``signedPayload`` to a
server that is making the access decision where the signature can be validated and results read directly. The
alternative where making an on device decision is to read from the ``insight`` incorporate those into
decision logic within the app.

However the result is consumed ``reportConsumption(_:insightsUsed:)`` should be called to indicate the usage made of the insights.

declarations.name: InsightEvaluator.ModelVersion
declarations.comment:
Defines the version of the insight that is required.

Nomally
``InsightEvaluator/InsightContext/InsightRequest/Version/current`` is the correct
 choice and specific older versions should only be requested if there is a particular need to either run an
 older version in parallel with the with the lates version or regulatory requirements mean that the a specific
 version must be used.

 Please see documentation for information about available models and policies regarding availability of specific
 models.

declarations.name: InsightEvaluator.OperationCategory
declarations.comment:
The type of operation that the assessment is being done for. This is important for usage transparency information
and may also have an affect on the behaviour of the evaluation that may affect the InsightResult values

A message based on this may be displayed to users in transparency logs showing app usage of Insights

declarations.name: IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight
declarations.comment:
Insight to request indications that the user may be actively being coached to perform actions
it could be useful to consider this in operations where it is possible that the user may be being
defrauded (e.g. transfers to new counterparties) and whether step ups or blocks may be
appropriate. Be aware that coaching may not necessarily be malicious.
